::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What measure can we use by LaTeX to control the print budget](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/31268/what-measure-can-we-use-by-latex-to-control-the-print-budget), asked by [pythonee](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/7848/pythonee) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-10-11; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I found there are so much excellent answer to questions about how to product high quality typesetting output. But I wonder how to save ink with LaTeX. What we need to think about to manage cost. page layout or something else?
:::

You can use [Ecofont Vera Sans][1], which has tiny holes cut out of the glyph strokes to use less ink:

![ecofont][2]

Ecofont is part of a software package that creates this effect on all your fonts.  But it only works in MS Office on Windows.  

Century Gothic is another light font that uses less toner per glyph than average.

  [1]: http://www.ecofont.com/en/products/green/font/download-the-ink-saving-font.html
  [2]: Xvj0u.jpg
